review.title: Locksmith work order records
review.plain: A person who makes a key to a home or business for someone else by onsite inspection must record the buyer's name, address, ID and other details on a work order and keep it two years; violating this is a misdemeanor.
acts: makes a key capable of opening any door or other means of entrance to any residence or commercial establishment for another
violates any provision of this subdivision

penalties.penalty: A misdemeanor (no term is stated in this section)

crimes.act: Makes a key capable of opening any door or other means of entrance to any residence or commercial establishment for another by any method involving an onsite inspection of such door or entrance, and violates any provision of this subdivision
conditions: The person does not obtain on a work order form, together with the date the key was made, the street address of the residence or commercial establishment, and the signature of the person for whom the key was made, the name, address, telephone number (if any), date of birth, and driver's license number or identification number (if any) of the person requesting or purchasing the key; or does not retain a copy of each such work order for two years open to inspection by any peace officer or by the Bureau of Collection and Investigative Services during business hours or submitted to the bureau upon request
exceptions: Nothing in this section prohibits the duplication of any key for a residence or commercial establishment from another such key
intent: Knowingly and willfully
terms: "Making of a key": includes, but is not limited to, the making of a key from key codes or impressions

review.title: Code grabbing devices
review.plain: Possessing a code grabbing device, or using one to disarm a vehicle security alarm, with intent to use it in an unlawful act is a misdemeanor.
acts: possesses a code grabbing device
uses a code grabbing device to disarm the security alarm system of a motor vehicle

penalties.penalty: A misdemeanor (no term is stated in this section)

terms: "Code grabbing device": a device that can receive and record the coded signal sent by the transmitter of a motor vehicle security alarm system and can play back the signal to disarm that system

crimes.act: Possesses a code grabbing device
intent: With the intent to use it in the commission of an unlawful act

crimes.act: Uses a code grabbing device to disarm the security alarm system of a motor vehicle
intent: With the intent to use the device in the commission of an unlawful act

review.title: Sniperscopes
review.plain: Knowingly buying, selling, receiving, disposing of, concealing, or possessing a sniperscope (an infrared night-vision firearm attachment) is a misdemeanor punishable by up to one year in county jail and a $1,000 fine.
acts: buys, sells, receives, disposes of, conceals, or has in his possession a sniperscope

crimes.act: Buys, sells, receives, disposes of, conceals, or has in his possession a sniperscope
exceptions: Authorized use or possession by a member of the armed forces of the United States or by police officers, peace officers, or law enforcement officers authorized by the properly constituted authorities for the enforcement of law or ordinances
Use or possession when used solely for scientific research or educational purposes
terms: "Sniperscope": any attachment, device or similar contrivance designed for or adaptable to use on a firearm which, through the use of a projected infrared light source and electronic telescope, enables the operator thereof to visually determine and locate the presence of objects during the nighttime

penalties.penalty: A misdemeanor punishable by a fine not to exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000) or by imprisonment in the county jail for not more than one year, or by both such fine and imprisonment

review.title: Unauthorized keys to public buildings
review.plain: Knowingly making, duplicating, using, or possessing a key to a state, county, city, or public school building or area without authorization is a misdemeanor.
acts: makes, duplicates, causes to be duplicated, or uses, or attempts to make, duplicate, cause to be duplicated, or use, or has in his possession any key to a building or other area owned, operated, or controlled by the State of California, any state agency, board, or commission, a county, city, or any public school or community college district

crimes.act: Makes, duplicates, causes to be duplicated, or uses, or attempts to make, duplicate, cause to be duplicated, or use, or has in his possession any key to a building or other area owned, operated, or controlled by the State of California, any state agency, board, or commission, a county, city, or any public school or community college district
ways: attempts to make, duplicate, cause to be duplicated, or use
conditions: Without authorization from the person in charge of such building or area or his designated representative
knowledge: With knowledge of the lack of such authorization

penalties.penalty: A misdemeanor (no term is stated in this section)

review.title: Forgery defined
review.plain: Forgery is signing another's name, forging a seal or handwriting, falsifying official records, or making or passing false checks, bonds, deeds, and other listed documents, with intent to defraud; the punishment is set in Section 473.
acts: signs the name of another person or of a fictitious person to any of the items listed in subdivision (d)
counterfeits or forges the seal or handwriting of another
alters, corrupts, or falsifies any record of any will, codicil, conveyance, or other instrument
falsely makes, alters, forges, or counterfeits, utters, publishes, passes or attempts or offers to pass, as true and genuine, any of the following items
falsifies the acknowledgment of any notary public
issues an acknowledgment

penalties.penalty: No punishment is stated in this section

crimes.act: Signs the name of another person or of a fictitious person to any of the items listed in subdivision (d)
intent: With the intent to defraud
knowledge: Knowing that he or she has no authority to do so

crimes.act: Counterfeits or forges the seal or handwriting of another
intent: With the intent to defraud

crimes.act: Alters, corrupts, or falsifies any record of any will, codicil, conveyance, or other instrument, the record of which is by law evidence, or any record of any judgment of a court or the return of any officer to any process of any court
intent: With the intent to defraud

crimes.act: Falsely makes, alters, forges, or counterfeits, utters, publishes, passes or attempts or offers to pass, as true and genuine, any of the following items: any check, bond, bank bill, or note, cashier's check, traveler's check, money order, post note, draft, controller's warrant, county order or warrant, request for the payment of money, receipt for money or goods, bill of exchange, promissory note, order, assignment, contract, due bill, passage ticket, lottery ticket or share purporting to be issued under the California State Lottery Act of 1984, trading stamp, power of attorney, certificate of ownership or other document evidencing ownership of a vehicle or undocumented vessel, stock certificate, or other listed instrument; or falsifies the acknowledgment of any notary public; or any matter described in subdivision (b)
ways: falsifies the acknowledgment of any notary public
intent: With the intent to defraud
knowledge: Knowing the same to be false, altered, forged, or counterfeited

crimes.act: Issues an acknowledgment

review.title: Forging a driver's license or ID card
review.plain: Altering, forging, copying, or counterfeiting a government-issued driver's license or ID card to help commit forgery is punishable by up to one year in county jail or as a felony.
acts: alters, falsifies, forges, duplicates or in any manner reproduces or counterfeits any driver’s license or identification card issued by a governmental agency

crimes.act: Alters, falsifies, forges, duplicates or in any manner reproduces or counterfeits any driver's license or identification card issued by a governmental agency
intent: With the intent that such driver's license or identification card be used to facilitate the commission of any forgery

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in a county jail for not more than one year, or imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170

review.title: Possessing a forged driver's license or ID
review.plain: Displaying or possessing a driver's license or ID card of the kind in Section 470a, intending it to be used to commit forgery, is punishable by up to one year in county jail or as a felony.
acts: displays or causes or permits to be displayed or has in his or her possession any driver’s license or identification card of the type enumerated in Section 470a

crimes.act: Displays or causes or permits to be displayed or has in his or her possession any driver's license or identification card of the type enumerated in Section 470a
ways: causes or permits to be displayed
has in his or her possession
intent: With the intent that the driver's license or identification card be used to facilitate the commission of any forgery

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in a county jail for not more than one year, or imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170

review.title: Forging record entries
review.plain: Making, forging, or altering an entry in a book of records, or a record or return named in Section 470, with intent to defraud is forgery; the punishment is set in Section 473.
acts: makes, forges, or alters any entry in any book of records, or any instrument purporting to be any record or return specified in Section 470

penalties.penalty: No punishment is stated in this section

crimes.act: Makes, forges, or alters any entry in any book of records, or any instrument purporting to be any record or return specified in Section 470
intent: With intent to defraud another

review.title: Falsifying medical records
review.plain: Altering or modifying a person's medical record, or creating a false medical record, with fraudulent intent is a misdemeanor.
acts: alters or modifies the medical record of any person
creates any false medical record

penalties.penalty: A misdemeanor (no term is stated in this section)

intent: With fraudulent intent

crimes.act: Alters or modifies the medical record of any person
Creates any false medical record

review.title: Forging public or corporate seals
review.plain: Forging or counterfeiting a state, court, public officer's, or corporate seal or its impression, or possessing and concealing a known counterfeit seal, with intent to defraud is forgery; the punishment is set in Section 473.
acts: forges, or counterfeits the seal of this State
falsely makes, forges, or counterfeits any impression purporting to be an impression of any such seal
has in his possession any such counterfeited seal or impression thereof

penalties.penalty: No punishment is stated in this section

intent: With intent to defraud another

crimes.act: Forges, or counterfeits the seal of this State, the seal of any public officer authorized by law, the seal of any Court of record, or the seal of any corporation, or any other public seal authorized or recognized by the laws of this State, or of any other State, Government, or country
Falsely makes, forges, or counterfeits any impression purporting to be an impression of any such seal
Has in his possession any such counterfeited seal or impression thereof and conceals the same
intent: With intent to defraud another
Willfully conceals

review.title: Punishment for forgery
review.plain: Forgery is punishable by up to one year in county jail or as a felony; forgery of a check or similar item worth $950 or less is limited to one year in county jail unless the person has certain prior convictions.
acts: Forgery
guilty of forgery relating to a check, bond, bank bill, note, cashier’s check, traveler’s check, or money order

crimes.act: Commits forgery

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in a county jail for not more than one year, or imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170

crimes.act: Commits forgery relating to a check, bond, bank bill, note, cashier's check, traveler's check, or money order
conditions: The value of the check, bond, bank bill, note, cashier's check, traveler's check, or money order does not exceed nine hundred fifty dollars ($950)
exceptions: This subdivision shall not be applicable to any person who is convicted both of forgery and of identity theft, as defined in Section 530.5

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in a county jail for not more than one year

penalties.if: the person has one or more prior convictions for an offense specified in clause (iv) of subparagraph (C) of paragraph (2) of subdivision (e) of Section 667 or for an offense requiring registration pursuant to subdivision (c) of Section 290
penalties.penalty: May instead be punished pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170

review.title: False telegraph or telephone messages
review.plain: Sending, delivering, or furnishing a false or forged message purporting to come from a telegraph or telephone office or another person, to deceive, injure, or defraud, is punishable by up to one year in county jail or as a felony, and a $10,000 fine.
acts: sends by telegraph or telephone to any person a false or forged message
delivers or causes to be delivered to any person any such message
furnishes, or conspires to furnish, or causes to be furnished to any agent, operator, or employee

intent: With the intent to deceive, injure, or defraud another

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in a county jail not exceeding one year, or imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170, or a fine not exceeding ten thousand dollars ($10,000), or both that fine and imprisonment

crimes.act: Sends by telegraph or telephone to any person a false or forged message, purporting to be from a telegraph or telephone office, or from any other person
intent: Knowingly and willfully
With the intent to deceive, injure, or defraud another

crimes.act: Delivers or causes to be delivered to any person any such message falsely purporting to have been received by telegraph or telephone
intent: Willfully
With the intent to deceive, injure, or defraud another

crimes.act: Furnishes, or conspires to furnish, or causes to be furnished to any agent, operator, or employee, to be sent by telegraph or telephone, or to be delivered, any such message
knowledge: Knowing the same to be false or forged

review.title: Possessing forged or blank checks
review.plain: Possessing or receiving forged items, or possessing blank or completed checks, money orders, and similar items, intending to complete, pass, or utter them to defraud, is forgery; the punishment is set in Section 473.
acts: possesses or receives
possesses any blank or unfinished check, note, bank bill, money order, or traveler’s check, whether real or fictitious
possesses any completed check, money order, traveler’s check, warrant or county order, whether real or fictitious

penalties.penalty: No punishment is stated in this section

crimes.act: Possesses or receives any forged, altered, or counterfeit items, or completed items contained in subdivision (d) of Section 470
intent: With the intent to pass or facilitate the passage or utterance
With intent to defraud
knowledge: Knowing the same to be forged, altered, or counterfeit

crimes.act: Possesses any blank or unfinished check, note, bank bill, money order, or traveler's check, whether real or fictitious
intent: With the intention of completing the same or the intention of facilitating the completion of the same, in order to defraud any person

crimes.act: Possesses any completed check, money order, traveler's check, warrant or county order, whether real or fictitious
intent: With the intent to utter or pass or facilitate the utterance or passage of the same, in order to defraud any person

review.title: Fictitious or altered checks
review.plain: Making, passing, or possessing a fictitious or altered bill, note, or check of a real or fictitious financial institution, with intent to defraud, is forgery; the punishment is set in Section 473.
acts: makes, passes, utters, or publishes
attempts to pass, utter, or publish
has in his or her possession

penalties.penalty: No punishment is stated in this section

crimes.act: Makes, passes, utters, or publishes, or attempts to pass, utter, or publish, any fictitious or altered bill, note, or check, purporting to be the bill, note, or check, or other instrument in writing for the payment of money or property of any real or fictitious financial institution as defined in Section 186.9
ways: attempts to pass, utter, or publish
intent: With intent to defraud any other person

crimes.act: Has in his or her possession any fictitious or altered bill, note, or check, purporting to be the bill, note, or check, or other instrument in writing for the payment of money or property of any real or fictitious financial institution as defined in Section 186.9
intent: With like intent to utter, pass, or publish
With intent to defraud any other person

review.title: Bad checks (insufficient funds)
review.plain: Writing or delivering a check knowing there are not enough funds or credit to cover it, with intent to defraud, is punishable by up to one year in county jail or as a felony; $950 or less is generally county jail only.
acts: makes or draws or utters or delivers a check, draft, or order upon a bank or depositary, a person, a firm, or a corporation, for the payment of money

crimes.act: Makes or draws or utters or delivers a check, draft, or order upon a bank or depositary, a person, a firm, or a corporation, for the payment of money
conditions: For himself or herself, as the agent or representative of another, or as an officer of a corporation
Although no express representation is made with reference thereto
intent: Willfully, with intent to defraud
knowledge: Knowing at the time of that making, drawing, uttering, or delivering that the maker or drawer or the corporation has not sufficient funds in, or credit with the bank or depositary, person, firm, or corporation, for the payment of that check, draft, or order and all other checks, drafts, or orders upon funds then outstanding, in full upon its presentation
terms: "Credit": an arrangement or understanding with the bank or depositary, person, firm, or corporation for the payment of a check, draft, or order
consequences: A sheriff's department, police department, or other law enforcement agency may collect a fee from the defendant, not exceeding twenty-five dollars ($25) for each bad check, in addition to the amount of any bank charges incurred by the victim (bank charges reimbursed to the victim may not exceed ten dollars ($10) per check)

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in a county jail for not more than one year, or pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170

penalties.if: the total amount of all checks, drafts, or orders that the defendant is charged with and convicted of making, drawing, or uttering does not exceed nine hundred fifty dollars ($950) (not applicable if the defendant has previously been convicted of three or more violations of Section 470, 475, or 476, or of this section, or of petty theft in a case in which the offense was also such a violation, or of a like offense under the laws of any other state or of the United States)
penalties.penalty: Punishable only by imprisonment in the county jail for not more than one year

penalties.if: the total does not exceed nine hundred fifty dollars ($950) and the person has one or more prior convictions for an offense specified in clause (iv) of subparagraph (C) of paragraph (2) of subdivision (e) of Section 667 or for an offense requiring registration pursuant to subdivision (c) of Section 290
penalties.penalty: May instead be punished pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170

review.title: Counterfeiting coin or bullion
review.plain: Counterfeiting gold or silver coin, gold dust, or bullion, or knowingly selling or passing such counterfeits, with intent to defraud, is counterfeiting; the punishment is set in Section 478.
acts: counterfeits any of the species of gold or silver coin current in this State, or any kind or species of gold dust, gold or silver bullion, or bars, lumps, pieces, or nuggets
sells, passes, or gives in payment such counterfeit coin, dust, bullion, bars, lumps, pieces, or nuggets
permits, causes, or procures the same to be sold, uttered, or passed

penalties.penalty: No punishment is stated in this section

intent: With intention to defraud any person

crimes.act: Counterfeits any of the species of gold or silver coin current in this State, or any kind or species of gold dust, gold or silver bullion, or bars, lumps, pieces, or nuggets
Sells, passes, or gives in payment such counterfeit coin, dust, bullion, bars, lumps, pieces, or nuggets, or permits, causes, or procures the same to be sold, uttered, or passed
ways: permits, causes, or procures the same to be sold, uttered, or passed
knowledge: Knowing the same to be counterfeited

review.title: Punishment for counterfeiting
review.plain: Counterfeiting is punishable by two, three, or four years of imprisonment under subdivision (h) of Section 1170.
acts: Counterfeiting

crimes.act: Commits counterfeiting

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170 for two, three or four years

review.title: Possessing counterfeit coin or bullion
review.plain: Possessing or receiving counterfeit gold or silver coin, gold dust, or bullion intending to pass it, knowing it is counterfeit and intending to defraud, is punishable by two, three, or four years under subdivision (h) of Section 1170.
acts: has in his possession, or receives for any other person, any counterfeit gold or silver coin of the species current in this state
permits, causes or procures the same to be sold, uttered or passed

intent: With intention to defraud any person
knowledge: Knowing the same to be counterfeit

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170 for two, three or four years

crimes.act: Has in his possession, or receives for any other person, any counterfeit gold or silver coin of the species current in this state, or any counterfeit gold dust, gold or silver bullion or bars, lumps, pieces or nuggets
intent: With the intention to sell, utter, put off or pass the same
With intention to defraud any person

crimes.act: Permits, causes or procures the same to be sold, uttered or passed

review.title: Counterfeiting equipment
review.plain: Making or knowingly possessing dies, plates, machines, or other things used to counterfeit coin, bullion, or bank notes is punishable by two, three, or four years under subdivision (h) of Section 1170, and the equipment must be destroyed.
acts: makes
has in his or her possession any die, plate, or any apparatus, paper, metal, machine, or other thing whatever

crimes.act: Makes, or has in his or her possession any die, plate, or any apparatus, paper, metal, machine, or other thing whatever, made use of in counterfeiting coin current in this state, or in counterfeiting gold dust, gold or silver bars, bullion, lumps, pieces, or nuggets, or in counterfeiting bank notes or bills
ways: has in his or her possession
consequences: All dies, plates, apparatus, papers, metals, or machines intended for the purpose aforesaid must be destroyed
If the counterfeiting apparatus or machine is a computer, computer system, or computer network, it shall be disposed of pursuant to Section 502.01
terms: "Computer, computer system, or computer network": include any software or data residing on the computer, computer system, or computer network used in a violation of this section ("computer system" and "computer network" have the meaning specified in Section 502)

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170 for two, three, or four years

review.title: Forging railroad or steamship tickets
review.plain: Counterfeiting, forging, or altering a railroad or steamship ticket or pass, or circulating one with intent to defraud, is punishable by up to one year in county jail or as a felony, and a $1,000 fine.
acts: counterfeits, forges, or alters any ticket, check, order, coupon, receipt for fare, or pass
utters, publishes, or puts into circulation, any such counterfeit or altered ticket, check, or order, coupon, receipt for fare, or pass

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in a county jail, not exceeding one year, or imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170, or fine not exceeding one thousand dollars, or both that imprisonment and fine

crimes.act: Counterfeits, forges, or alters any ticket, check, order, coupon, receipt for fare, or pass, issued by any railroad or steamship company, or by any lessee or manager thereof, designed to entitle the holder to ride in the cars or vessels of such company
Utters, publishes, or puts into circulation, any such counterfeit or altered ticket, check, or order, coupon, receipt for fare, or pass
intent: With intent to defraud any such railroad or steamship company, or any lessee thereof, or any other person

review.title: Counterfeit transit fare media
review.plain: Counterfeiting, forging, or altering public transit fare media is punishable by up to one year in county jail or state prison; knowingly possessing it, or passing fare media to defraud, is up to one year in county jail.
acts: counterfeits, forges, or alters any fare media designed to entitle the holder to a ride on vehicles of a public transportation system
possesses any counterfeit, forged, or altered fare media
utters, publishes, or puts into circulation any fare media

crimes.act: Counterfeits, forges, or alters any fare media designed to entitle the holder to a ride on vehicles of a public transportation system, as defined by Section 99211 of the Public Utilities Code, or on vehicles operated by entities subsidized by the Department of Transportation

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in a county jail, not exceeding one year, or in the state prison (no state prison term is stated in this section)

crimes.act: Possesses any counterfeit, forged, or altered fare media designed to entitle the holder to a ride on vehicles of a public transportation system, as defined by Section 99211 of the Public Utilities Code, or on vehicles operated by entities subsidized by the Department of Transportation

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in a county jail not exceeding one year, or a fine not exceeding one thousand dollars ($1,000), or both that imprisonment and fine

crimes.act: Utters, publishes, or puts into circulation any fare media
intent: With intent to defraud

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in a county jail not exceeding one year, or a fine not exceeding one thousand dollars ($1,000), or both that imprisonment and fine

review.title: Restoring canceled tickets
review.plain: Removing cancellation marks from a used railroad or steamship ticket or pass to reuse, sell, or defraud, or knowingly offering such a restored ticket, is punishable by up to six months in county jail and a $1,000 fine.
acts: removes, conceals, fills up, or obliterates, the cuts, marks, punch-holes, or other evidence of cancellation
offers for sale, or in payment of fare on the railroad or vessel of the company, such ticket, check, order, coupon, or pass

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the county jail not exceeding six months, or a fine not exceeding one thousand dollars, or both such imprisonment and fine

crimes.act: Removes, conceals, fills up, or obliterates, the cuts, marks, punch-holes, or other evidence of cancellation, from any ticket, check, order, coupon, receipt for fare, or pass, issued by any railroad or steamship company, or any lessee or manager thereof, canceled in whole or in part
intent: For the purpose of restoring to its original appearance and nominal value in whole or in part
With intent to dispose of by sale or gift, or to circulate the same, or with intent to defraud the railroad or steamship company, or lessee thereof, or any other person

crimes.act: Offers for sale, or in payment of fare on the railroad or vessel of the company, such ticket, check, order, coupon, or pass
intent: With like intent to defraud
knowledge: Knowing the same to have been so restored, in whole or in part

review.title: Selling nontransferable transit tickets
review.plain: Selling a ticket, pass, or other instrument for passage on a common carrier for use by someone not entitled to use it under its terms is a misdemeanor.
acts: sell to another any ticket, pass, scrip, mileage or commutation book, coupon, or other instrument for passage on a common carrier

crimes.act: Sell to another any ticket, pass, scrip, mileage or commutation book, coupon, or other instrument for passage on a common carrier
conditions: For the use of any person not entitled to use the same according to the terms thereof, or of the book or portion thereof from which it was detached
exceptions: Except as otherwise provided in Section 26002.5 of the Government Code and Sections 40180.5 and 99151 of the Public Utilities Code

penalties.penalty: A misdemeanor (no term is stated in this section)

review.title: Deceptive identification documents
review.plain: Making or selling fake-looking ID documents without a "NOT A GOVERNMENT DOCUMENT" mark, knowing they will be used to defraud, is punishable by up to one year in county jail or as a felony; possessing document-making devices is a misdemeanor.
acts: violates the provisions of subdivision (a)
violates the provisions of subdivision (b)

terms: "Deceptive identification document": any document not issued by a governmental agency of this state, another state, the federal government, a foreign government, a political subdivision of a foreign government, an international government, or an international quasi-governmental organization, which purports to be, or which might deceive an ordinary reasonable person into believing that it is, a document issued by such an agency, including, but not limited to, a driver's license, identification card, birth certificate, passport, or social security card

"Document-making device": includes, but is not limited to, an implement, tool, equipment, impression, laminate, card, template, computer file, computer disk, electronic device, hologram, laminate machine or computer hardware or software
consequences: Any person who violates or proposes to violate this section may be enjoined by any court of competent jurisdiction, in actions prosecuted by the Attorney General, any district attorney, or any city attorney

crimes.act: Manufactures, sells, offers for sale, furnishes, offers to furnish, transports, offers to transport, or imports or offers to import into this state a deceptive identification document
conditions: The document does not bear, diagonally across its face, in not less than 14-point type and printed conspicuously in permanent ink, the statement NOT A GOVERNMENT DOCUMENT and, also printed conspicuously, the name of the manufacturer
knowledge: Knows or reasonably should know that the deceptive identification document will be used for fraudulent purposes

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in a county jail not to exceed one year, or imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170

crimes.act: Possesses a document-making device
intent: With the intent that the device will be used to manufacture, alter, or authenticate a deceptive identification document
consequences: Any document-making device may be seized by law enforcement and shall be forfeited to law enforcement or destroyed by order of the court upon a finding that the device was intended to be used to manufacture, alter, or authenticate a deceptive identification document

penalties.penalty: A misdemeanor punishable by imprisonment in a county jail not exceeding one year, or a fine not exceeding one thousand dollars ($1,000), or both imprisonment and a fine

review.title: Theft defined
review.plain: Defines theft (stealing, embezzling, or obtaining property by false pretenses), sets how the value of property and services is measured, and creates presumptions of intent for unreturned leased or rented property.

review.title: False information to pawnbrokers
review.plain: Knowingly giving false information about your identity, ownership, or authority to sell property to get money from a pawnbroker or secondhand dealer, and receiving it, is theft; the court may also order restitution.
acts: gives false information or provides false verification as to the person’s true identity or as to the person’s ownership interest in property or the person’s authority to sell property
receives money or other valuable consideration from the pawnbroker or secondhand dealer

crimes.act: Gives false information or provides false verification as to the person's true identity or as to the person's ownership interest in property or the person's authority to sell property, and receives money or other valuable consideration from the pawnbroker or secondhand dealer
conditions: The person receives money or other valuable consideration from the pawnbroker or secondhand dealer
intent: In order to receive money or other valuable consideration from a pawnbroker or secondhand dealer
consequences: The court may require restitution to the pawnbroker or secondhand dealer in an amount not exceeding the actual losses sustained
The probation officer, if one is assigned, shall notify the pawnbroker or secondhand dealer or coin dealer of the time and place of the sentencing hearing

penalties.penalty: Guilty of theft (no punishment is stated in this section)

review.title: Diverting construction funds
review.plain: Receiving money for construction services, labor, or materials and willfully diverting it to another use is punishable by up to one year in county jail or as a felony, and a $10,000 fine, if over $2,350; otherwise a misdemeanor.
acts: receives money for the purpose of obtaining or paying for services, labor, materials or equipment
fails to apply such money for such purpose
diverts the funds to a use other than that for which the funds were received

crimes.act: Receives money for the purpose of obtaining or paying for services, labor, materials or equipment and fails to apply such money for such purpose, and diverts the funds to a use other than that for which the funds were received
ways: failing to complete the improvements for which funds were provided
failing to pay for services, labor, materials or equipment provided incident to such construction
intent: Willfully
Wrongfully

penalties.penalty: A misdemeanor when the amount diverted is less than or equal to two thousand three hundred fifty dollars ($2,350) (no term is stated in this section)

penalties.if: the amount diverted is in excess of two thousand three hundred fifty dollars ($2,350)
penalties.penalty: A fine not exceeding ten thousand dollars ($10,000), or imprisonment in a county jail not exceeding one year, or imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170, or both that fine and that imprisonment

review.title: False vouchers for construction loans
review.plain: Submitting a false voucher to get construction loan funds and not using the funds for the stated purpose is embezzlement.
acts: submits a false voucher to obtain construction loan funds

crimes.act: Submits a false voucher to obtain construction loan funds and does not use the funds for the purpose for which the claim was submitted
conditions: The person does not use the funds for the purpose for which the claim was submitted

penalties.penalty: Guilty of embezzlement (no punishment is stated in this section)

review.title: Access card definitions
review.plain: Defines "cardholder," "access card," "card issuer," "retailer," "counterfeit access card," "traffic," "card making equipment," and related terms for the access card crimes in Sections 484e to 484j.

review.title: Access card theft
review.plain: Selling or transferring someone's access card without consent, acquiring cards in four or more names in a year, or taking card account information to use fraudulently is grand theft; holding a card to misuse it is petty theft.
acts: sells, transfers, or conveys, an access card
acquires access cards issued in the names of four or more persons
acquires or retains possession of an access card
acquires or retains possession of access card account information with respect to an access card validly issued to another person

crimes.act: Sells, transfers, or conveys, an access card
conditions: Without the cardholder's or issuer's consent
intent: With intent to defraud

penalties.penalty: Guilty of grand theft (no punishment is stated in this section)

crimes.act: Acquires access cards issued in the names of four or more persons
crimes.who: A person other than the issuer
knowledge: Has reason to know the cards were taken or retained under circumstances which constitute a violation of subdivision (a), (c), or (d)

penalties.penalty: Guilty of grand theft (no punishment is stated in this section)

crimes.act: Acquires or retains possession of an access card
conditions: Without the cardholder's or issuer's consent
intent: With the intent to defraud
With intent to use, sell, or transfer it to a person other than the cardholder or issuer

penalties.penalty: Guilty of petty theft (no punishment is stated in this section)

crimes.act: Acquires or retains possession of access card account information with respect to an access card validly issued to another person
conditions: Without the cardholder's or issuer's consent
intent: With the intent to use it fraudulently

penalties.penalty: Guilty of grand theft (no punishment is stated in this section)
